title: Heterogeneous-link-aware Handoff Calibrator for multi-GPU prefill-decode
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We see increased p99 tail latency and throughput variance on clusters that mix NVLink-connected racks and PCIe-only nodes. Current prefill/decode handoff timing assumes uniform inter-GPU comm latency and uses a fixed rendezvous offset. With heterogeneous links this causes comm stalls, kernel misalignment, and backpressure that increases overall latency and degrades throughput stability.

Goal: Implement a runtime 'handoff calibrator' that measures link characteristics (latency, sustained bandwidth, transfer setup cost) at task startup and dynamically computes token handoff offsets and kernel affinity hints to smooth NCCL/collective overlap across heterogeneous topologies. The calibrator should integrate with kernel selection hints and the prefill-decode scheduler so that communication windows are sized and phased to maximize overlap without causing stalls.

Approach:
- Lightweight probe at pod/worker init: micro-benchmarks for point-to-point latency and small/large collective throughput across peer set (sampling, not exhaustive).
- Model: per-connection estimates (setup_cost, bandwidth, jitter). Aggregate into per-stage expected transfer time distribution.
- Handoff calibration algorithm: compute stagger offsets per-stage (ms) and kernel-affinity suggestions (prefer local fused-kernels when link latency high) to shift prefill chunks so decode work on downstream GPUs starts after expected KV/weight transfers have been seeded.
- Integration points: scheduler receives calibrator output, applies per-request dynamic offset and priority for kernel election (low-latency paths favor aggressive prefetch; high-latency links favor larger prefetch/batching and conservative kernel choices).
- Fallbacks: if probes fail or topology changes mid-epoch, revert to current adaptive-stagger strategy; log telemetry and trigger a quick re-probe.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Probe frequency vs. overhead: single probe per deployment/epoch vs. continuous probes with exponential backoff when performance deviates. We opt for single warmup probe + event-triggered re-probe to limit noise.
- Complexity of per-request offsets: per-request offsets increase scheduler complexity and slightly increase latency variance for very short requests; we threshold application only when sequence length or token budget justifies.
- Kernel affinity hints are advisory; we will not enforce hard kernel switches mid-request to avoid state churn.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Cluster-level baseline: reduce 99th percentile latency for mixed-link clusters by >= 12% on our perf harness for Llama-like 8k token streams.
2) Throughput stability: reduce variance (stdev) of tokens/sec across workers by >= 18% under realistic arrival patterns.
3) Safety: no degradation >2% in median latency on homogeneous NVLink-only clusters.
4) Telemetry: per-stage handoff offset and probe metrics are emitted and visible in Console.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for probe parser and calibrator math.
- Integration harness runs on multi-topology testbed (NVLink pairs + PCIe nodes) including synthetic congestion.
- A/B rollout on Dedicated with canary traffic (10% traffic, pinned to test pool) for 48h before ramp.

Telemetry/observability: emit probe timestamps, measured setup_cost/bandwidth, computed offsets, kernel-affinity suggestion, and a calibration confidence score. Surface anomalies as alerts (calibration_confidence < 0.5 or re-probe > 3x in 10 minutes).

Rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime-1.22. Start with internal Dedicated test clusters, then opt-in enterprise customers for private trials, then wider Dedicated rollout if metrics meet acceptance criteria.

Notes: This ticket focuses strictly on calibrator + scheduler integration. Subsequent ticket will be created to expose fine-grained user controls (max-offset, probe cadence) in Console and to run long-term telemetry-driven auto-tuning.
